doc.title: Eddie Marshall interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002

title: Uncle Gilley Roberts and the trad band
summary: His 104-year-old uncle Gilley Roberts played banjo with Louis Armstrong; Marshall played in a trad band at colleges in the fifties.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: RPI. I have an uncle who is still living, Gilley Roberts, he’s a banjo player who played with Louis Armstrong in 1927, and went to Europe with him and everything. Gilley is 104. And one of my other jobs, he was in the family too, it was another band I played in, we had a traditional jazz band. And we worked all the colleges, like all the fancy colleges, Amherst and University of Massachusetts and all the Upstate schools, and just playing trad music. And this was like in the fifties. And we would make like sometimes two hundred and three hundred dollars a week back in those days, playing at those — Rensselaer, what’s the famous womens’ school that’s in — Vassar. And they would lock us in and lock us out. They were so protective of their women.
They kept a tight— right. Well best of luck.
Well I hope this is good, I’ve got to get going myself.
